stocks.investment_thesis: Intel delivered a transformational Q1 2026 beat — revenue of $13.58B vs. $12.42B expected, non-GAAP EPS of $0.29 vs. $0.01 consensus — marking its sixth consecutive quarter of exceeding guidance, driven by a 22% surge in Data Center & AI revenue and early traction for its 18A manufacturing node. Q2 guidance of $13.8B–$14.8B is materially above the prior consensus of ~$13.04B, validating the Q2 supply recovery thesis Esten flagged as a precondition in March. The core bear-case risk — that supply constraints and sub-35% gross margins would suppress the story — has partially resolved, but valuation at ~$99 is now severely stretched relative to any fundamental anchor, with the stock up +151% YTD and trading at RSI ~87, well into overbought territory.

stocks.bull_case: Intel has delivered its sixth consecutive earnings beat with the strongest revenue and margin upside in years. DCAI is growing at 22% YoY, AI-driven revenue surged ~40% YoY, and advanced packaging is emerging as a multi-billion dollar incremental revenue stream. Supply constraints are easing into Q2 as guided. Tesla confirmed as Intel 14A's first external customer. Multiple firm upgrades post-earnings (Evercore ISI to Outperform, $111 target; HSBC to Buy, $95; Citi to Buy). US CHIPS Act tailwinds and geopolitical demand for domestic semiconductor capacity provide structural support. Google committed to multi-generation Intel CPU adoption. The CPU is resurging as the 'indispensable foundation of the AI era' per CEO Lip-Bu Tan. From Esten's March entry price of ~$45, the position has already returned +120%, so existing holders are well in profit.
stocks.bear_case: The stock has surged ~+300% in 12 months and +151% YTD, reaching all-time highs near $100. RSI at 87–88 is deeply overbought. GuruFocus GF Value pegs intrinsic value at ~$27.99 (255% overvalued); Alpha Spread base-case DCF at ~$33.83. Fwd P/E is likely 100–161x depending on estimate vintage, not the 66.4x shown in the email — far above any reasonable semiconductor peer. GAAP net loss widened to -$4.28B in Q1 despite the non-GAAP beat. Intel Foundry operating loss remains -$2.4B/quarter. Free cash flow was -$2.0B in Q1. 18A yield not expected to reach industry-standard levels until 2027. External foundry revenue is tiny ($174M in Q1). Consensus analyst target is ~$63–79, materially below current price. Management guided PC demand to weaken in H2 2026. The stock is now priced for near-flawless multi-year execution.

thread_narrative: Esten's single-line email flags Intel's Q1 2026 earnings beat and Q2 guidance well above consensus, noting a +17% after-hours move. This is a terse factual alert rather than an analytical research note — it contains no updated price target, no revised buy/sell recommendation, and no thesis evolution commentary. The email serves primarily as a timely trigger alert for a position Esten has tracked since March 2026, when he issued a WAIT_FOR_DIPS at $45 with a score of 52/10, contingent on evidence of Q2 supply recovery and 18A yield improvement. Both conditions have now materially shown up in the Q1 results: supply constraints are easing into Q2, 18A yield targets have reportedly been pulled forward to mid-year, and non-GAAP gross margin of 41% is 650bps above guidance and well clear of the sub-35% floor that made the original risk/reward unattractive. The broker's track record on this name is exceptional — the WAIT_FOR_DIPS at $45 has returned +120% in roughly six weeks. However, the fundamental landscape has shifted dramatically: the stock is now at all-time highs near $100, trading at an RSI of ~87 and well above the analyst consensus target of $63–79, with a fwd P/E likely 100–161x. The email's listed fwd P/E of 66.4x appears stale and materially understated. The investment case at $99 is categorically different from the case at $45 — the margin of safety is gone and the stock is pricing near-flawless execution through 2027–2028.

For a stock outside the broker's core Nordic universe and now at dramatically elevated valuation, a follow-up note with explicit guidance on whether to add, hold, or take profits at current levels is critically needed.
